- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after initial spikes.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Late-period forecasts (last 5–10 days) are generally too low, indicating underestimation of downward momentum or delayed correction.
- Forecasts exhibit lagged behavior — true values often dip below forecasted values after a spike, suggesting model reacts too slowly to market shifts.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, underestimating volatility or downward pressure.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10 days — suggesting asymmetric bias toward overconfidence in early trends.
